name: Women's Street Safety Perception in Dalian
description: Method replication: same task, scales and design as the paper; the images are not the paper's stimuli (168 new Baidu street views, four directions at 42 points within about 500 m of the Xi'an Road / Changjiang Road junction in Shahekou District, Dalian, captured 2019–2023). Original study: Li, Wu, Xue & Jiang (2025), Buildings 15(18): 3310, doi:10.3390/buildings15183310. The authors sampled 146 points at 100 m intervals around Xi'an Road and took street views at 0°, 90°, 180° and 270° (584 images). 32 female volunteers, selected because they had no experience of harassment and had never visited the area, saw each photo for 20 s in randomised order and rated street safety from two perspectives, built-environment safety and behavioural-activity safety, on five levels (0–19, 20–39, 40–59, 60–79, 80–100). Each volunteer rated the first 50 photos; a random-forest model then predicted the rest. Age, education, income and occupation were recorded. Differences from the original study: (1) the points come from a grid within about 500 m of the junction, not 100-m points on the OpenStreetMap network; (2) each participant rates 50 photos drawn at random from the 168, and there is no human-machine model predicting further photos; (3) the 20 s viewing is enforced by unlocking the ratings after 20 s; (4) the two question wordings and their hints are ours, based on the paper's description of the two perspectives; (5) whether the participant has visited the area is asked rather than used to screen people out, and the separate 160-person on-site questionnaire is not included.
author: Li, Wu, Xue & Jiang
